annotations.text:
What came from where.

From the Cerca kit: the name, "Start with fit, not availability", the language rules, the white-label ratio, and Clients in the navigation.

Changed: the accent moved off green. An olive brand beside a green "positive" means a user cannot tell whether green means Cerca or good — the same fault, one layer down. Terracotta is complementary to teal, so the two can never be confused.

Dropped: the blue, the five-token semantic set (those hexes were stock design-system tokens, not designed for this), Inter, and the good-fit-rate metric.

Every question on one page. Not step 2 of 5.

The Cerca kit proposed one question at a time. Your own brief records the opposite as a tested decision — stepwise felt like an interrogation, which is precisely what this product exists not to be.

So: one page, with a fixed Continue bar carrying progress, because at 390px "all on one page" is a long scroll and people need to know how much is left.

Multi-booking, driven by a balance.

Six left, three chosen — the cap is what they paid for, not a form limit. "Same time every week" comes first because most ten-session programmes are exactly that, and picking ten slots by hand on a phone is a chore.
